lesson: One winner is a channel, not a niche.

name: Stone Explainer

name: Through the Ages
why: [N] 2026-10-28: 'Through the Ages is an AI slop channel. Like it's AI videos. Like it's not a good channel to make with Claude.'

name: Map Mayhem
why: [N] 2026-10-28: 'map mayhem is also barely getting views… it's low rpm since it looks gamey quiz like for kids.'
lesson: Quiz, guessing and kid-game looks are refused however good the ratio; check the whole cluster's size.

name: Hank Green
why: [K3] 'We don't want to use this big channel… this is skewed data'; Hank Green at 3.2M subs is 'bad data… out of the window'.
lesson: Big channels' numbers don't transfer to a new channel.

name: 425-sub one-hit (from the c7-cem6Zypo video)
why: [K3] 'only one video went viral. We want a repeated formula.'
lesson: A single viral video on a tiny channel is not proof.

name: 'AI automation just died' channels
lane: old-style YouTube automation (stock footage, default AI voice, top-10 facts)
why: [K2] A 1M-subscriber automation channel now gets about 1.5K views a video; 'you could swap your video with a competitor's and nobody would notice'.
lesson: Swappable, mass-produced content is dead: the look and the subject must be ownable.

name: Zack D. Films copycats
lane: everyday objects in 3D (Zack D. Films wake)
why: [N] 2026-10-28: Zack D. Films at 16M per Short plus small copycats that are one- or two-hit wonders (Thanks Dave 5.5M + 616K then 3–51K; Oak Light 2.2M + 904K on a 17K median).
lesson: A giant's wake isn't a cluster of winners: read the small channels' medians.

name: Ryoga
lane: anime-drawn fitness ('How to force your X to grow')
why: [D] The owner's model BAD example in 'More Checks Is Better': banger to flop about 2:3. 'How To Force Your Skinny Arms To Grow' hit 1.7M and 'How I Forced My Shoulders To Grow' 265K, but the others sat at 10K-64K: random outliers, not a consistent format.
lesson: Judge the ratio, never the biggest video: one or two huge hits beside flops means the format isn't proven.
